subject: phoenix
reasoning:
I'm planning the phoenix model as a single TypeScript module, designing a standing pose with spread wings, fanned tail feathers, crest, and talons in warm flame colors, then setting up the skeleton hierarchy starting from the hips root.

I'm working out the spine chain as a Catmull path from hips through the chest to the neck and head, deciding where each joint sits spatially so the body sweep follows a natural upward curve before the neck chain branches off and parents to the last spine joint.

For the body shape, I'm sweeping along the spine chain with a radius function that's thinner at the hips, fattest at mid-body, then tapering toward the neck, plus a thinner separate neck sweep, using a countershaded red-to-gold paint for the body color. Then I'm starting to lay out the tail as its own chain branching backward and downward from the hips.

Now I'm working out the tail feathers: a fan of flattened bezier sweeps radiating from the tail tip, each with a narrow elliptical cross-section that tapers toward the tip, colored in bands shifting from red at the base through orange to a gold tip, oriented so they splay wide and flat in the horizontal plane.

Still adjusting tail feather heights...

Now I'm planning the wing joint chains per side, placing shoulder, elbow, wrist, and tip positions to create a spread, slightly-lifted rest pose, with each chain parented appropriately and labeled with a "wing" role.

For the primary feathers, I'm computing feather bases along the arm from elbow to wrist-tip, with each feather's direction and length tapering outward and backward to create the trailing wing shape.

I'll use `arm.at(t).bone` to safely attach the base point to the nearest joint. For feather shape, I'm setting width along x (perpendicular to the mostly-backward z direction) and keeping it thin vertically, with secondaries angled more inward and primaries spreading outward, plus a shorter covert layer underneath.

Now I'm planning the color gradients (red to orange to gold on primaries, gold to orange on coverts) and counting parts: roughly 40 for both wings, 11 for the tail. Then I'm moving to the head -- placing the head joint and sphere, and building the beak as upper and lower jaw cones attached to the head, oriented forward with a squashed scale for shape.

Still working out the beak geometry and jaw placement, then designing the eyes as small dark spheres with a gold ring behind them, positioned using local offsets on the head bone.

For the crest, I'm planning several feathers swept backward and upward from the top of the head using bezier curves, with each feather's base, mid, and tip points offset laterally to fan them out, needing a small helper to build these point vectors cleanly.

For the legs, I'm sketching a bird-style three-segment limb (hip to knee to hock to foot) using fixed length and bend arrays to approximate the characteristic bird leg shape.

Adding toe rods and claw spikes...

For chest plumes, I'm scattering small outward-pointing cones on the body surface to create a spiky, flame-like feather effect, filtering by normal direction so they only appear on upper-facing areas.

Actually, I think cards with an SVG feather texture would look nicer -- designing a two-layer feather shape in orange and gold gradient to place along the chest hits.

Scattering those feather cards along the body sweep with a bit of random variation and a backward lean should give a decent plume effect, plus adding similar ruff cards around the neck. I'll keep the head simple without extra effects like a flame halo, and just make sure the body and neck sweeps connect cleanly along their bone chains.

Working out the taper so the neck emerges naturally from the body's chest without an awkward seam -- shrinking the body's end radius and defining a radius function that bulges in the middle like a plump chest tapering to narrower hips and shoulders, then checking where the legs should start showing below the body silhouette.

Setting up the neck chain with two joints parented to the spine, and positioning the head joint at the neck's tip with a forward-angled direction so it reads as looking up and out. Building the spine chain with a curved path from hips through the chest, then starting the tail chain curving backward from the hips.

Now I'm defining the jaw joint and beak geometry: a lower cone angled slightly down-forward and an upper cone angled more steeply to create a hooked beak shape, positioning the head sphere to sit just behind where the beak joins.

I'm setting up the color palette (reds, oranges, gold, dark, beak, leg tones) and defining the body's paint pattern using a mottled red-orange texture with a countershaded gold underside. Now I'm starting the wing construction loop, defining a chain of points sweeping outward from the shoulder for each side of the body.

Writing wing feather logic...

Still shaping feather geometry...

Setting up color bands for the feathers and realizing the spacing along the arm will cause heavy overlap, so I'll offset each feather vertically to layer them properly.

Working out the covert feathers next — 9 of them with gradient coloring, plus the tail feathers where the central ones are longest, tapering outward with alternating curvature for depth.

Still defining tail geometry... deciding to skip eyespot decals, and planning to scatter chest and neck card decorations on the body above a height threshold.

Now I'm setting card density to 60 with minimum spacing, and moving into writing the export code itself, starting with a helper function for vector addition along a direction.
